jobs.title: Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning
Sr. Developer Advocate, AI and Machine Learning

reading.body:
The entire developer relations and education slice of AI hiring in this data is one Databricks job, a senior developer advocate role, posted twice on the same day for San Francisco and Seattle.

Two records, identical title, identical posting date, same employer, two cities. That reads as a single requisition opened in two offices rather than two distinct hiring needs, so the count of two overstates distinct demand by half. Both are senior, both sit in major West Coast metros, and neither is remote.

Developer relations is the adoption layer of the AI software stack, the people who teach outside developers to build on a platform. It sits far from physical constraints. Nothing in these two records concerns data centers, power, or chips, so this function offers no evidence either way on whether compute or the grid binds AI scaling. It is a signal about platform adoption, not about capacity.

The source list covers federal openings, European listings, remote boards, and aggregators, but both records arrived through a company career board. What is captured is what one employer chose to post publicly, not the market. A single employer's two postings cannot establish a trend, and the absence of other companies is not evidence that they are not hiring. The postings are roughly a month old relative to the build date, so either may already be filled. There is no salary, no seniority detail beyond the title, and no outcome.
